entities.summary: Infante Sancho of Castile was a pivotal figure in the 13th-century Christian Reconquista, serving as Archbishop of Toledo and Chancellor of Castile from 1259 until his death in 1261. As a key leader in the Catholic Church, Sancho played a crucial role in the unification of the Iberian Peninsula, securing the region for Christian rule and paving the way for the eventual expulsion of the Moors. Sancho's legacy extends beyond his own time, influencing the course of Western civilization and shaping the modern nation-state of Spain. The city of Toledo, where Sancho held his archbishopric, remains a testament to his enduring impact on the region's history and culture. Through his diplomatic efforts and strategic alliances, Sancho successfully navigated the complex web of medieval politics, earning him a lasting place in the annals of Spanish history. Despite the limitations of his time, Sancho's vision for a unified and Christianized Iberia left an indelible mark on the region, shaping the trajectory of European history for centuries to come.
